extracted.intended_audience: journal reviewers and editors in academic publishing
extracted.subtask_description: High-level principles and concrete recommendations for how individual peer reviews and peer review processes for journal manuscripts should be conducted to ensure quality, integrity, fairness, usefulness, and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 1 — Content Integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: A review must engage with the substance of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on the research question and aims; comment on the methods and analyses, including reproducibility; comment on the interpretation of findings and whether claims are warranted; identify strengths as well as weaknesses; detect statistical, factual, or logical errors; check for adequate citation of prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 2 — Content Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are custodians of research integrity and must flag ethical problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag suspected research misconduct (fabrication, falsification, plagiarism, image manipulation); identify undeclared conflicts of interest; identify ethical concerns (informed consent, animal welfare, sensitive populations, dual-use research); flag redundant publication or salami slicing; maintain manuscript confidentiality and do not appropriate ideas, data, or methods; decline review when an unmanageable conflict of interest exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 3 — Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews and editorial decisions must be impartial and respectful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge manuscripts on scientific merit, not author identity (institutional, gender, geographic, language); apply the same standards across submissions (avoid double standards by reputation); use constructive, professional language and avoid sarcasm or personal attack; avoid demanding citations to the reviewer's own work unless genuinely necessary (anti-coercive citation); provide balanced assessments with proportional strengths and weaknesses; consider alternative interpretations of the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 4 — Usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should help authors and editors improve the work and make decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific comments (line/page references rather than blanket criticisms); substantiate comments with reasoning, evidence, or examples; be constructive — explain how to fix problems, not only that something is wrong; distinguish major from minor concerns and prioritise them; provide a clear recommendation consistent with the review narrative; tailor language for author readability (avoid jargon-only critiques).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 5 — Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must meet time expectations so the editorial process proceeds efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly to review invitations (accept or decline within 7 days); decline rather than delay if you cannot meet the deadline; submit reviews on or before the deadline; notify the editor as soon as you anticipate delay; do not hold up subsequent rounds — respond to revision rounds at least as quickly as the first round.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt structured review forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use structured review templates that map to the five principles to ensure coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structured forms should explicitly prompt reviewers to address content integrity, ethics, fairness, usefulness, and timeliness so that each principle is enforced in the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reviewer training
rubrics_metrics.description: Train reviewers on the five principles and recommended practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer training for new reviewers and ongoing education so reviewers understand how to implement content integrity, content ethics, fairness, usefulness, and timeliness in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use transparent peer review where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider publishing review reports and reviewer identities by mutual agreement to incentivise good practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparent peer review can encourage constructive behaviour and accountability, but should be implemented with attention to consent and context-specific appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Give credit to reviewers for their contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise reviewers using systems such as ORCID and Publons/Web of Science Reviewer Recognition to acknowledge reviewer work and incentivise quality reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors should monitor reviewer quality (use instruments like RQI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial oversight should track and assess reviewer performance and review quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should monitor reviewer quality using instruments such as the Reviewer Quality Index (RQI) to identify training needs, reward good reviewers, and ensure adherence to the five principles.
